findings.title: Midnight timestamps silently become whole-day bounds
findings.description: The `date | datetime` union parses `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` as a `date`, verified with FastAPI/Pydantic. `resolve_window()` consequently expands this explicit end timestamp to `23:59:59.999999`, returning an extra day of data. Midnight timestamps with offsets also lose their timezone. Both routes are affected. Preserve the distinction between bare dates and timestamps, and add midnight/offset regression tests.

findings.title: Large responses block the event loop
findings.description:
Only database reads run in the executor; model construction and serialization execute synchronously inside the async handler. An isolated benchmark using the actual candle model code at 75,000 rows took approximately **749 ms to build and 306 ms to dump**, excluding encoding. This blocks other requests and violates the required sub-millisecond synchronous-work bound. Trades have the same pattern at lines 166–174.

Offload construction and serialization after releasing the connection. Add a load test measuring lightweight-request latency while a ceiling-sized response is generated; concurrent market-detail requests alone do not exercise this failure.

Project tests could not run because the available Python environments lack `psycopg`.
